Conditional Tenses Review

You use conditionals in English to describe the consequence of an action in a real or hypothetical situation. Also, you can explain the situations that might have happened in the past. The zero and first conditionals are the ones used in the present and future tenses.

You use the zero conditional to talk about something that is always true in the present. The condition causes a result which is always true.

To write a sentence using the zero conditional you must use the following structure:

If + simple present + comma + simple present

Example:

If you want to learn how to program this software, you have to study hard.

 You use the first conditional to talk about a possible situation in the future, the condition happens in the present and it has a consequence in the future.

To use the first conditional remember to use the following structure:

If + simple present + comma + future simple

Example:

If you learn how to use Java, you will be able to work in lots of platforms.
If we make a short list based on the popularity of the programming languages, you will have a clearer idea about them.
If you want to learn something that is cost-effective and easy to learn, your best option is Java.
Modal Verbs Review
We use modal verbs to express possibility, ability, permission or obligation.

Modal verbs are used as an auxiliary verb that helps modifying the main verb on the sentence. We use them in different situations and for different purposes. Here are some of the modal verbs organized by their function:

Understanding the Importance of Choosing Words Carefully and Correctly
When you write a text, it is important to know which words to use or which ones would be more appropriate for the kind of text you're writing.

If you choose inappropriate words or expressions, your reader might not understand you, or they may understand something different to what you want to say. You must make sure you use the correct words, choosing them carefully to express exactly what you mean.

In order to do it, you might want to use of two common objects: a dictionary and a Thesaurus.

A dictionary will help you find the definition of the word you want to use, division into syllables, part of speech and some examples of how to use the word.

Example:

Pa•per•back (ˈpeɪ•pərˌbæk), noun: a book with a cover made of thick paper.
I want to get a paperback to read on the plane

​A thesaurus is also useful because you can find words with similar meanings to the one you're trying to use, or if you cannot find the right word for what you mean, then a thesaurus will find it for you.

Example:

Architect, noun. Artist, builder, creator, designer, engineer, inventor, planner.

Kate: Hey Jack! What are you doing?
Jack: Nothing much, I'm skimming this website about the most efficient programming languages because I want to study one of these next year, but it seems like I might not be able to make a choice right now.
Kate: Let me take a look. Alright, this website elaborates on several features for each one. If we make a short list based on the popularity of the programming languages, you will have a clearer idea about them.

Jack: Okay, let's do it. Ranking by popularity my short list might go something like this:
    1. Java
    2. C
    3. C++
    4. Python
    5. Assembly

Kate: Good. So, according to the website, if you want to learn something that is cost-effective and easy to learn, your best option is Java.
Jack: But I previously studied Java, what would you recommend?

Kate: I like C++ better; I feel it is more efficient for me, because of its speed; so if you want to work with better memory usage and speed, C or C++ are the best options you have. Then again, if you haven't got enough time, you should learn something that appeals to you; like Python for example, which is also easy to learn. Or if you are interested in a challenge, try Assembly which may be hard to learn and work with, but you might like it, who knows? My advice would be for you to find out what kind of software you want to write. If you like what you are learning, then it will feel more pleasant and not like something you're forced to learn.
Jack: You're right, this helped me a lot. Thanks, Kate!
